BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to state institutions; amending RCW 71A.20.020 and72.23.020; adding a new section to chapter 41.06 RCW; adding a newsection to chapter 72.05 RCW; adding a new section to chapter 72.16RCW; adding a new section to chapter 72.19 RCW; adding a new section tochapter 72.20 RCW; adding a new section to chapter 72.40 RCW; adding anew section to chapter 72.36 RCW; adding a new section to chapter28A.150 RCW; adding a new section to chapter 72.09 RCW; adding a newchapter to Title 43 RCW; and creating a new section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature finds that stateinstitutions serve a critical role in the delivery of services andlong-term residential care for the people of the state of Washington.Maintaining the capital needs and assessing the need for efficiencies,consolidation, expansion, reduction, closure, and replacement of stateinstitutions requires both longterm planning and financing. A fair,objective, and factual assessment of the capital facilities is acritical part of how to best meet the needs of the clients of theinstitutions and the citizens of Washington. However, the state lacksan independent review process and an effective method of decision p. 1 HB 1584making for state institutions with excess capacity or with alternativeservice delivery models to meet state policy. The legislature furtherfinds that independent evidence-based facts are crucial to any decisionthat affects Washington citizens who reside in state institutions; andthat a fair and objective analysis of the independent evidencebasedfacts will be better for the clients of the institutions. For these reasons, the legislature intends to create aninstitutions review commission as an independent entity to review stateinstitutions on a regular basis.

The definitions in this section applythroughout this chapter unless the context clearly requires otherwise. (1) "Commission" means the institutions review commission createdunder section 3 of this act. (2) "Commissioner" means a member of the commission created undersection 3 of this act. (3) "Immediate family member" means the parents, spouse, siblings,children, or dependent relative of the official, employee, or lobbyistwhether or not living in the household of the official, employee, orlobbyist. (4) "Lobbyist" means a person registered as a lobbyist underchapter 42.17 RCW. (5) "Public official" means any person holding federal, state,county, city, town, school district, port district, special district,or other state political subdivision elective office. (6) "Review cycle" means the period beginning July 1st of an oddnumbered year and ending December 1st of the following evennumberedyear. (7) "State institution" means residential habilitation centers,state institutions for juvenile offenders, state hospitals, the stateschool for the deaf, the state school for the blind, the department ofcorrections, the department of veterans affairs, and facilitiesassociated with the Washington national guard youth challenge programpursuant to RCW 28A.150.305.

The institutions review commission isestablished to review the effectiveness of and the need for stateinstitutions. HB 1584 p. 2 (1) The ninemember commission must be appointed as follows: (a) By July 1, of 2007, and by July 1st of each oddnumbered yearthereafter, the two largest caucuses of each house of the legislatureshall each appoint one commissioner. The governor shall appoint fivecommissioners. (b) Commissioners serve two-year terms expiring July 1st of eachoddnumbered year. Commissioners may be reappointed, subject to theconditions of this section. (c) The commission members shall be appointed based on geographicrepresentation of the state. (d) The following persons are ineligible for appointment to thecommission: (i) Persons who reside in a legislative district where aninstitution that is scheduled for review during that review cycle islocated; (ii) State officials, public employees, representatives of unionsthat represent public employees, lobbyists, and immediate familymembers of such officials, employees, representatives, or lobbyists. (e) Upon a vacancy in any position on the commission, the originalappointing authority must appoint a successor to fill the unexpiredterm within thirty days. (2) Commissioners may not receive compensation for their services,but shall receive a subsistence allowance and travel expenses under RCW43.03.050 and 43.03.060. (3) The commissioners shall elect a chair from among their members.

(1) The commission shall investigate, makefindings of fact, and make determinations about the efficiency of theinstitutions reviewed, including but not limited to the decisionwhether to consolidate, expand, close, replace, or retain aninstitution under review. (2) The commission is authorized to access state information anddata regarding institutions, and state agencies shall cooperate withthe commission in its efforts to collect data. (3) The commission shall hold at least one public hearing regardingeach institution under review within the vicinity of the facility underreview. p. 3 HB 1584 (4) Based on its review, the commission shall determine whether toconsolidate, expand, reduce, close, replace, or retain a stateinstitution. The commission shall provide its decisions to thegovernor and the appropriate policy and fiscal committees of thelegislature before December 1st of each evennumbered year.

In conducting its review of stateinstitutions and in making its decision to consolidate, expand, reduce,close, replace, or retain an institution, the commission shall considercriteria including but not limited to the following: (1) The best quality of care for the institution's residents basedon state laws and policies regarding care and treatment, includingcommunity care and treatment, for clients and potential clients of theinstitutions; (2) The condition of the institution's physical plant and the needfor repair or renovation; (3) The institution's location relative to population centers,supporting services, persons served, and families of persons served; (4) The best and highest use of the institution's property; (5) The costs of providing service at that institution relative tolike institutions and community care or treatment; and (6) State duties, objectives, and policies as expressed in law orin formally adopted agency policies.

(1) Unless the legislature, by a twothirdsvote of each house, rejects or revises the decision in law, thecommission's decision to consolidate, expand, reduce, close, replace,or retain an institution takes effect the July 1st following the end ofthe review cycle, and the governor and the various state agencies shallimplement the commission's decisions. (2) The authority granted to the commission to consolidate, reduce,close, replace, or retain an institution is supplemental to and inaddition to any powers granted to the governor as a management right.
During the 200708 review cycle, thecommission shall review the state school for the blind and the stateschool for the deaf and report its decisions by December 1, 2008.

The commission shall review all stateinstitutions at least once during the five consecutive review cyclesthat begin July 1, 2007. By May 31, 2009, and each oddnumbered year thereafter, thecommission shall designate the institutions to be reviewed in thefollowing review cycle by the subsequently appointed commissioners.

The commission has the following powers andduties in addition to any other powers and duties authorized orrequired by law. The commission: (1) Shall employ an executive director, who serves at thediscretion of the commission, and other staff as are necessary toimplement the purposes of this chapter; (2) May make, execute, and deliver contracts, conveyances, andother instruments necessary to exercise and discharge its powers andduties; (3) May contract for all or part of the services necessary for themanagement and operation of the commission with other state or nonstateentities authorized to do business in the state; and (4) May contract with consultants as necessary to carry out itsresponsibilities.
